data.title: COMT rs4680 polymorphism modulates openness to experience in women with alcohol
data.text: PMID 42898859: "COMT rs4680 polymorphism modulates openness to experience in women with alcohol use disorder." (Postep Psychiatr Neurol, 2026). Abstract: PURPOSE: The objective of the study was to examine the association between COMT rs4680 genotypes, alcohol use disorder diagnosis, and differences in Five-Factor personality traits. METHODS: We examined 213 adult women in total, including 101 with a diagnosis of alcohol use disorder (AUD) and 112 non-addicted controls. All participants completed the NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI) and were genotyped for the COMT rs4680 polymorphism using real-time PCR. Group comparisons and genotype × diagnosis interactions were analyzed using ANOVA and post hoc tests. RESULTS: Women with AUD scored significantly higher on Neuroticism and Openness to Experience, and lower on Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Conscientiousness compared to controls. data.text: PMID 42889467: "Association of stress-related genetic risk and lifestyle factors with BMI in Korean adults." (Nutr Res Pract, 2026). Abstract: Association of stress-related genetic risk and lifestyle factors with BMI in Korean adults.. BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Genetic susceptibility to stress may influence behavioral and metabolic responses involved in dietary choices and body weight regulation. While previous studies have focused on individual genetic variants related to dietary intake and obesity risk, a polygenic approach integrating multiple stress-related single nucleotide polymorphisms may better capture overall genetic susceptibility to stress. This study examined the relationship among stress-related polygenic risk, dietary intake, serum metabolite profiles, and body weight, and determined whether this relationship could be influenced by sleep duration and physical activity (PA). SUBJECTS/METHODS: This study included 100 disease-free participants with a body mass index (BMI) of 18.5 to 25.0 kg/m2. data.title: Grounded Interpretation
data.content:
The variant rs4680 in the COMT gene is classified as benign by ClinVar. It is associated with potential differences in response to certain drugs, such as buprenorphine, fentanyl, and tramadol, and may influence the severity of nicotine withdrawal and the response to propranolol. However, the evidence for these associations is not clinically actionable and other genetic and clinical factors may also play a role.

**Limitations:**
- Ensembl could not be reached; this report is partial.
- Ensembl VEP data was unavailable due to an issue with Ensembl.
- The evidence for the associations with drug response and personality traits is not strong and may be influenced by other factors.
